## What is being simulated, and why

## Serially first

The version that is slow and obviously correct, kept because everything after it has to agree with it.

## Across the cores you have

One line changed, using `future::plan(multicore)`. The timing quoted with the session size, as a single run rather than a benchmark.

## Was that enough?

The honest checkpoint. If the analysis finishes here, the section should say so and stop, rather than reaching for the cluster to complete a demonstration. Doing that in a worked example is more persuasive than asserting it on a task page.

## If it was not enough

Where `spark_apply()` comes in, what the call looks like for this analysis, and the caveats carried from [What changes when the data is not on your laptop](../concepts/index.qmd) rather than restated: two workers observed, nothing claimed about scaling, and the `columns` argument omitted so the example works from either context.

If the replicates do spatial work, `sf` has to load in the worker too, which depends on the library situation described in [Packages](../ref/packages.qmd). If it is not available, this stage of the example does not run, and the page should say that plainly rather than assume.
